content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day window.
- Forecast shows upward trend but fails to capture sharp downward spikes in true values (e.g., after 86+ peaks).
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves in history (e.g., 86.87 → forecast jumps to 88+).
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects downward after high peaks, then fails to rebound.
- Forecast lags true values by 1–3 days in the first 10 days, then catches up or diverges later.
- Model overestimates volatility in early days, underestimates in late days — suggests horizon-dependent calibration error.
- True values often dip below 80 after 15–20 days, while forecast remains above 85 — indicates failure to model long-term mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to be smoother than true values, missing abrupt drops or spikes in the last 5–10 days.
